content.comment_body: Hi, I'm trying to show countdown timer information from an Off-Delay Function in [product_name] on a Kinco HMI. It's easy to display in the text box of [product_name], but I can't figure out how to show it on an HMI panel. Any advice?
Hello, Have you seen this link: How do you connect a [product_name] [article_no] and an HMI panel? Best regards, [user_name]
You need to use the Parameter-VM-Mapping function, which is found in [product_name] software under the Tools menu.
Here’s a link to a PDF from the Kinco website: [url]

Thanks, I know how to set up and display functions and switches both ways between Kinco HMI and [product_name], but I can't figure out how to push timer info to the HMI. It's easy on the [product_name] panel, but I haven't managed on the HMI. I'd like something like: Dosing started at: 12:00:00 Ending in 12:02 mins Thanks, [user_name]

Hi, An external device doesn't have direct access to parameters of a [product_name] program (except for its dedicated panel). To make them available, you need to publish the internal parameters to the VM memory of [product_name] using VM-mapping. In the mapping table, select the appropriate function block and memory location, such as VW0. Then your HMI can read from that memory location to display the data. There's a reference image showing how this looks in your VM mapping table. Hope this helps.
Great! Thank you for your help!
Hello, I'm trying to connect Kinco HMI with [product_name] version 8. I believe I can do this using an ethernet cable. Please assist.
If you think ethernet will work, have you read through all the posts in this topic?
You only need to create a connection in the HMI. If you have further questions, please ask them specifically. General statements like "I'm a newbie" aren't very helpful.
Thank you. For the download, I need a username and password. What should I do?
Which download do you mean? My PDF? There shouldn’t be a password required.
Yes, your PDF. I’ve already logged in, but it still requests a username and password for the download.
Are you trying to log in from the [company_name] web page to download the PDF? From my side, there’s no login required.
All I can provide is a screen video of what I see.

Hi, It seems you’re having a download issue due to something installed on your computer. The pop-up about "saving the password in IDM password list" suggests checking your IDM (Internet Download Manager) settings. This problem might occur with other websites too.

It looks like they're using Internet Download Manager v6.38, which adds compatibility for Windows 10 and various browsers including Internet Explorer 11, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and Google Chrome.

analysis.insight_summary: Users struggle to display timer countdown data from an Off-Delay function in [product_name] on an external Kinco HMI. While viewing on the dedicated panel is straightforward, showing this data on third-party HMI requires exporting internal parameters to VM memory addresses via VM-Mapping in [product_name] configuration software. This setup is not obvious to users unfamiliar with the process.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects to easily show countdown timer information from [product_name] on a third-party HMI, similar to the experience on the built-in panel, and hopes for a simple configuration or data transfer process for timer parameters.
